The Fairer Test

Scope up front. Reported domestic nonstop flights operated by UA/19977 and WN/19393; United Express and other codeshare operators excluded. Comparable flights share a directional airport route, normalized local scheduled departure date and departure window; common scheduled-count weights. Each operator is scored against its own timetable unless a different deadline is explicitly named. This is operator-only performance on comparable flights, against each operator’s own published arrival timetable.

Tied on Paper

The amended question is whether United beats Southwest by more than two points on comparable flights.

The amended, registered question. National averages mix different routes and departure times. A common basket asks a narrower question.

Replicated

In 2023–2024, United-operated comparable flights completed less than 15 minutes late against their own schedules 6.27 percentage points more often than Southwest-operated flights: nominal 99% missingness envelope [4.60, 7.94] points. Verdict: UA advantage above two points.

In 2025, United-operated comparable flights completed less than 15 minutes late against their own schedules 8.20 percentage points more often than Southwest-operated flights: nominal 99% missingness envelope [5.31, 11.00] points. Verdict: UA advantage above two points.

The registered decisive label repeats in both periods: replicated. A was sealed before B was opened.

Registered words retained. UA = United-operated; WN = Southwest-operated. Channel owner approved the script and claims on 2026-10-09.

Only the registered A and B results decide their verdicts. Switching lenses cannot change either verdict. All registered sensitivities are descriptive and were not separately certified by the primary gate. Exploratory, post-hoc checks inherit no materiality verdict. For late-departure rates, a negative gap means fewer United late departures.

The registered envelope concerns repeated outcomes and calendar shocks on fixed schedules, using a 28-day studentized whole-network block method with 1,999 draws. It is neither historical census counting error nor a prediction for a future flight. The entire envelope must lie strictly above the line; equality is inconclusive. An entire envelope below it means “no material UA advantage under this rule.”

Exploratory, post-hoc · not registered

The timetable matters.

Using a shared midpoint elapsed-time allowance reduces the arrival gaps to 2.59 / 4.33 percentage points in A / B. United’s cancellation-inclusive timely-departure advantages are 9.91 / 13.28 points. Both checks use all scheduled flights as denominators.

United schedules 4.52 / 4.45 more block minutes in A / B. Its actual blocks are also 4.79 / 6.23 minutes longer on aligned cells with completed observations for both operators, covering 97.73 / 98.55% of comparison weight. Longer schedules do not identify unnecessary or intentional padding. The shared allowance starts at each flight’s scheduled departure; it is not one arrival clock or a causal share of the advantage.

Use the separate exploratory group in the lens selector to inspect the shared allowances, departure outcomes and local time bands. No added check changes the registered verdict.

How the comparison works

Give both operators the same basket.

“On time” means arriving strictly less than 15 minutes late against the operator’s own published timetable. Exactly 15 minutes late fails. Cancellations, diversions and indeterminate outcomes also fail; no failed service is removed because of its outcome.

What the data cannot tell us

A small slice. A precise question.

Own timetables

Matching route, date and departure window does not align arrival deadlines. Scheduled buffers and minute-level timing remain bundled with fleet, staffing, rotations and operating circumstances. The result measures timetable-promise performance, not common-clock speed or a cause.

United Express excluded

Only United-operated and Southwest-operated flights enter the contrast. Other operators flying under United’s brand are excluded. This is not a brand-wide quality ranking, connection-success measure or passenger-weighted comparison.

Small overlap

Comparable coverage is 11.91% / 11.16% of United-operated schedules and 6.22% / 6.33% of Southwest-operated schedules in A / B. A and B have separate frozen baskets. The estimate does not describe the unserved overlap or the whole network.

Denver-heavy

Denver touches 79.31% / 82.22% of comparison weight in A / B. Airport shares cannot be added: both endpoints can touch the same flight. Airport-omission and time-band lenses show why one average is not a universal advantage.

Heterogeneity remains

Early and late local departure bands differ substantially. Time-of-day checks are post-hoc, with no computed band intervals. A positive pooled result does not establish an advantage in every month, airport or time band.

Not a recommendation

These data do not identify the effect of choosing an airline, safety, fares, rebooking or eventual passenger arrival. This page is not airline-choice advice or a guarantee for a future trip.
